# K7.1 Parameter all-gather prefetch

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

`NVFP4_PREFETCH_PARAM_AG=1` (`config_GB300_2x4x3xtp1pp1cp1ep1_nvfp4_v7.sh` L130);
1 in G3, G6 and G6b and G6c. It needs Megatron's `overlap_param_gather`. The config sets `OVERLAP_PARAM_GATHER=True` and
`OVERLAP_PARAM_GATHER_WITH_OPTIM_STEP=False` (L173, L174).
The code is one `pretrain.py` block, the same text in all three (G3 L215–236, G6 and G6b L235–256, G6c L252–273). `pretrain.py` lines
below are G6/G6b; G3 is 20 lines lower, G6c 17 lines higher. Class: **Schedule**.

## 2. What the reference does

Megatron-LM `f6c33bde` `distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py`, `_ParamAndGradBucketGroup` (upstream; the file is not in
the package). With `overlap_param_gather`, a bucket group's parameter all-gather is issued asynchronously
(`start_param_sync`), and its handle is kept. The forward pre-hook of a parameter calls `finish_param_sync`, which waits on
that handle and then issues the next group's gather (`next_param_gather_bucket_group`). At most about one gather is
ahead of the compute.

## 3. What this implementation does

`_start_param_sync_prefetch` (L246–253) wraps `start_param_sync`. After the original call it walks
`next_param_gather_bucket_group` and calls the original `start_param_sync` for every group not yet dispatched (L250–253).
All remaining gathers of the step are therefore queued behind the first one the forward issues. It does nothing for
`force_sync` or without `overlap_param_gather` (L248–249). Megatron's warning about the next bucket's gather being
already dispatched is silenced (L256). `finish_param_sync` is not changed.

## 4. Why the result is the same

The same collectives on the same inputs into the same outputs; only the issue time changes.

- **Disjoint outputs:** each group's all-gather writes its own buckets' slices of the param buffer (the comment at
  L236–239 states this; the bucket layout is Megatron's and is not changed here).
- **Inputs final when issued:** the wrapper runs only from the forward, after the optimizer step. With
  `OVERLAP_PARAM_GATHER_WITH_OPTIM_STEP=False`, Megatron does not issue gathers inside the step. K1.4 issues its early
  gathers from inside the step through `_base_start_param_sync`, which is the unwrapped original (L335–337,
  `globals().get("_orig_start_param_sync")`). So no group is prefetched before its parameters are updated. An
  asynchronous NCCL collective is ordered after the work already queued on the issuing stream (PyTorch
  `ProcessGroupNCCL`, upstream behaviour), so the gathers read the updated shards.
- **Outputs complete before use:** every consumer still calls `finish_param_sync`, which waits on that group's own
  handle before the layer runs. The wrapper only issues; it never marks a handle done.
- **No overwrite of a pending gather:** the next writes to the param buffer are the next step's optimizer update. They
  come after the whole forward, in which every group was waited on.
- **Matching collectives:** the chain is the static `next_param_gather_bucket_group` list, so every rank issues the same
  sequence.

Schedule.

## 5. Numerics

None: no arithmetic. In G6 and G6b (and G6c) the gathered payload is K8.2's NVFP4 data, unchanged by the issue order.

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** switch 1, `overlap_param_gather` on, not `force_sync` (L235, L248).
- **Falls back:** the original one-at-a-time behaviour, silently, when `force_sync` is set or `overlap_param_gather` is off.
- **Assumes:** that no code issues `start_param_sync` for a group whose parameters are not yet updated. Today K1.4 is the
  only caller inside the step, and it uses the unwrapped function (L335–337). A new wrapper installed between them
  would prefetch stale shards without an error. It also assumes the NCCL communicator can hold all queued gathers
  (memory, not values).
- **Check:** config L130. The scored logs have no line from this block.

## 7. Code

- `nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/pretrain.py` L252–273. The wrapper order is FP4 all-gather (G6 L228–233, G6c L245–250, G6/G6b/G6c only), then
  prefetch, then K6.2's amax refresh (L260–293; G6c L277–310). The amax refresh therefore runs before the prefetch walk.

## 8. Tests and evidence

- **Module test, submitted image** (test `k1_4_k7_dp`): 12 BF16 linears in
  Megatron DDP + distributed optimizer configured as G6. The `pretrain.py` PREFETCH block runs as shipped. Grad buffers
  are prefilled with NaN; 6 steps × 2 micro-batches. Per step, the outputs and grad-buffer digests on every rank are
  compared with all switches off, and at the end the parameter bytes and optimizer state.
  - This package's image, job 22902 (DP8, two nodes; DP4 not run): `K7.1:prefetch` has 0 differing per-step outputs, grad
    buffers and final state, on every rank and in both runs. Run a vs b digests are equal. The cases that differ in
    these jobs belong to K7.2 and K1.4 fixtures (see those write-ups).
  - Job 22340 (G6 image, DP4) records the final state after a forced param sync: K7.1 0 differ.
- **Training A/B, G6 image:** job 22245 (`NVFP4_PREFETCH_PARAM_AG=0`) vs base 22243: max |loss diff| 0.1095 over 300
  steps, and base vs base 0.0873–0.1192 (runs are not bitwise repeatable).
